trace.topic: Dear SaaStr: At What Stage Should a Startup Hire a CMO?
trace.goal: Give stage-appropriate advice on when a startup really needs a CMO.
expected_facts: The answer should say that many startups hire a CMO too early.
It should explain that the role only works once there is enough repeatability and scope to justify it.
It should distinguish between tactical marketing needs and true CMO-level leadership.
rubric_must_haves: Explains what must already exist before the hire works.
Distinguishes leader type from function needs.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should say that founders usually need demand generation, product marketing, or content help before they need a true CMO. The CMO hire works when there is already enough scale, budget, and strategic complexity to support a full executive owner. Hiring one too early often creates expensive confusion instead of leverage.

trace.answer: Dear SaaStr: At What Stage Should a Startup Hire a CMO? Generally speaking, I recommend hiring your first marketing leader when you are ready for a full-time head of demand gen -- usually somewhere between $500k-$1m in ARR. This is because marketing can easily scale with minimal cost. As soon as you're ready to do more than just word-of-mouth marketing, you'll need someone dedicated to getting out there and bringing leads back into the funnel. If you haven't already, you should also hire a content marketer before this point. They will help create inbound interest and drive traffic to your site. Once you've established a strong foundation here, you can begin building upon it by hiring additional team members such as sales development reps, product marketers, brand managers, etc. Hiring too early in the process can actually hurt you since you won't have anything solid yet for them to work with. But once you see traction starting to build - especially after $1M ARR - then it might make sense to bring on a VP-level executive who can help take things to the next level.

https://quora.com/What-are-the-top-3-tasks-of-a-CMO-in-a-SaaS-startup-at-1M-ARR/answer/Jason-M.-Lemkin?share=c8726acf

Q:  When should a bootstrapped startup hire a (CFO, COO, CMO)? How can a CEO hire those C-level positions for the first time as a CEO and entrepreneur? What skills should he or she look for?
Here are some rough rules:
You want a VP of Everything (Sales, Marketing, Product, Eng) by about $1m-$2m ARR
. Not all at once, but you can benefit from all of them by then. A bit more
here
.
You want to start adding CXOs around $15m-$20m ARR
.
The CFO is often the last, the CMO often the first “C” level officer.
Now how does bootstrapping change this? Not that much. Certainly, it slows down how many VPs you can hire after $1m-$2m ARR. You probably have to hire them one at a time, a bit slowly.
But by $10m ARR, bootstrapped SaaS companies mint enough cash to fund all these hires. $10m ARR bootstrapped companies start to converge and look a lot like $10m ARR venutre-backed SaaS companies.  This is the key insight.  If you are bootstrapped in SaaS, you won’t have enough capital to build your management team as fast you need to for quite a while.  But as you approach $8m-$10m ARR, there will be enough revenue.  And no excuses not to have a fully built management team by then.
And thus the next level C-level hiring process ends up being about the same, bootstrapped or not.
IME, rough order to make hires in:
VPM: $0.2m ARR
VPS: $1-$1.5m ARR
VPCS: $2m ARR
VPP: $3m-$4m ARR
VPE:  $5m-$6m ARR
CFO: $10m ARR
COO: $20m ARR
